package_info.package_versions: 0.7.29, 0.8.0, 1.0.0 (ua-parser-js); similar pattern for coa and rc
package_info.why_malicious: These package versions were published after an account takeover and contained malicious files and a new preinstall script designed to execute malware (crypto miner and credential stealer) on user systems during installation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the preinstall script executes a malicious JavaScript file, which can perform arbitrary actions such as downloading and running additional malware, stealing credentials, or starting a crypto miner.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The addition of a preinstall script in a new version, especially when not present in previous versions, is a common vector for supply chain attacks. This script runs automatically on user machines during installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not add or modify install-time scripts without clear justification or documentation. Legitimate preinstall scripts are rare and usually well-documented.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use preinstall scripts for environment checks or setup, but these are typically transparent and documented.
key_indicators: Script executes external or untrusted code
No documentation or justification for the script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the malicious JavaScript downloads and executes a remote payload, which may install a crypto miner or credential stealer, exfiltrating sensitive data to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote code during installation is a hallmark of malware. This enables arbitrary code execution and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not download and execute remote code without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some legitimate tools auto-update or fetch binaries, but this is always documented and opt-in.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to maintainer account and publishes a new malicious version of the package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is added to the package.

attack_chain.action: Malicious preinstall script is triggered during package installation.
Malicious JavaScript downloads and executes additional payloads (crypto miner, credential stealer).
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, data exfiltration, or resource abuse.

behavioral_signatures: Addition of preinstall/install/postinstall scripts in new package versions
Scripts that execute external files or download remote code
Unexplained changes in package maintainers or release process
file_indicators: package.json with new or modified preinstall/install/postinstall scripts
Newly added JavaScript files not present in previous versions
Files that invoke shell commands or network requests
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified install-time scripts in package.json, especially in popular packages. Compare new releases to previous versions for unexplained script additions or new maintainers. Flag packages that download or execute remote code during installation. Alert on outbound network activity from npm install processes to untrusted domains.
